identity.description: Original single-seat, low-wing aerobatic trainer with a steerable tailwheel and fixed-pitch propeller.
identity.author: FlightCraft contributors

cl_clean.source: Original Prandtl lifting-line estimate: AR=8^2/11=5.82, section slope 2*pi, span efficiency 0.88 give a=4.52/rad, rounded to 4.6. Nearly symmetric section with CL0=0.04; assumed finite-wing CLmax=1.25 at 15.5 degrees. Separation reduces lift to 0.69 at 25 degrees; negative branch is reflected about CL=0.02. Textbook method: Anderson, Fundamentals of Aerodynamics, finite-wing theory; no measured aircraft data.

cl_flaps.source: Original thin-airfoil plain-flap estimate: 25-percent chord flaps over 45 percent of span, with effectiveness 0.55 at 16 degrees, yield delta CL approximately 2*pi*0.55*0.45*0.28=0.44; reduced to 0.35 for finite-span losses. Assumed CLmax=1.52 and earlier separation; no aircraft data.

cd_alpha.source: Original wetted-area build-up: turbulent skin friction 0.004 times wetted/reference area 4, plus 0.009 form, canopy, and fixed-gear drag gives CD0=0.025. Incidence pressure drag rises quadratically before separation; separated-flow endpoints are conservative assumptions. Induced drag is added separately with k=1/(pi*5.82*0.88)=0.0622.

cm_alpha.source: Original tail-volume build-up: a=4.6/rad and static margin 0.109 chord give Cm_alpha=-0.50/rad. Tail volume 0.42, tail slope 3.6/rad, efficiency 0.9, and downwash gradient 0.45 give tail contribution -0.75/rad, balanced by +0.25/rad wing/fuselage. Cm0=0.015 is an assumed rigging moment; statically stable with less margin than the Corvid.

cy_beta.source: Original vertical-tail build-up: tail area/wing area=0.12, tail slope 3.0/rad, and dynamic-pressure efficiency 0.9 give -0.324/rad; fuselage adds -0.156/rad, totalling CY_beta=-0.48/rad.

cl_beta.source: Original strip-theory estimate for a low wing with 2 degrees dihedral: -(4.6/4)*sin(2 degrees)=-0.040/rad, with -0.005/rad fuselage contribution. Cl_beta=-0.045/rad gives a restoring dihedral effect.

cn_beta.source: Original vertical-tail volume estimate: 0.12 area ratio times 2.8/8 arm/span times tail slope 3.0 times 0.9 efficiency =0.1134/rad, less 0.0184/rad fuselage destabilisation gives Cn_beta=0.095/rad.

aerodynamics.derivatives_source: Original textbook strip and tail-volume estimates (Etkin, Dynamics of Flight): Cl_p approximately -a/12=-0.38, increased to -0.42 for the tail; Cm_q=-2*0.9*3.6*0.42*(3.0/1.375)=-5.94, rounded to -6. Vertical-tail damping plus fuselage gives Cn_r=-0.20 and CY_r=0.22. Outboard ailerons spanning y/(b/2)=0.50..0.95, local lift increment 0.43, give Cl_delta=0.43*(0.95^2-0.50^2)/2=0.140. Elevator effectiveness 0.85 and rudder 0.09 are area/arm/travel build-ups; small cross derivatives are conservative design assumptions. Rates use pb/2V, qc/2V, rb/2V, controls full normalised travel.
